content.text: I audited every first-party source file in the repo (Eclipse Parsson — the `impl` core, the `rest` JAX-RS media providers, the `providers` test webapps, and the `demos`) and wrote `findings.json` in the repo root. No other files were modified. ## Finding (1) **Unescaped remote JSON interpolated into an HTML response** — `demos/rest/.../ParserResource.java:74`, CWE-79. The endpoint is `@Produces("text/html")` and builds HTML by hand. `farm`, `server`, `id`, and `secret` come straight from `JsonParser.getString()` and are concatenated into an `` tag with no HTML/attribute encoding and no numeric validation. The feed is fetched over cleartext `http://api.flickr.com/...` (line 53), so a network-position attacker or hijacked upstream fully controls the JSON body and thus the markup served to every visitor — a value like `">` escapes the attribute and the tag. ## What I checked and found clean - **Parser/tokenizer** (`JsonTokenizer`, `JsonParserImpl`): buffer index invariants hold (`storeEnd ≤ readBegin ≤ buf.length`, growth path doubles the buffer); the `\u` hex lookup is bounds-checked; raw control chars in strings are rejected; nesting depth, BigDecimal source length, and BigInteger scale limits are all enforced (`JsonContext`, `JsonTokenizer.getBigDecimal`, `JsonNumberImpl.bigIntegerValue`). - **Output escaping** (`JsonGeneratorImpl.writeEscapedString`, `JsonStringImpl.toString`): `"`, `\`, and all chars below 0x20 are escaped, so attacker-supplied strings cannot break out of JSON string context. - **JSON Pointer / Patch / Merge Patch** (`JsonPointerImpl`, `NodeReference`, `JsonPatchImpl`, `JsonMergePatchImpl`): token unescaping, array-index parsing, bounds checks, and the `move` proper-prefix check all behave as specified; pointers only traverse in-memory structures, so there is no filesystem or URL path involved. - **No sinks for the other requested classes exist in first-party code**: no SQL, no `Runtime.exec`/`ProcessBuilder`, no `ObjectInputStream`/`readObject` deserialization of untrusted bytes, no XML parsing at all (no XXE surface), no file paths or URLs built from caller input (the only outbound URLs are hard-coded demo endpoints), and no authentication/authorization logic. The `rest` `MessageBodyReader`/`Writer` and the three test servlets just delegate to the parser/generator. - **CI workflow** (`.github/workflows/pr.yml`): no untrusted `github.event.*` expressions interpolated into `run:` blocks. One caveat on scope: the finding is in demo code rather than the shipped library, and its exploitability depends on controlling the cleartext upstream response — I report it because the unescaped-HTML sink is real and in this repo's own code. The hard-coded Flickr API key on line 53 and the cleartext HTTP fetch are adjacent hygiene problems outside the categories you listed, so I noted them only as part of the attacker-control argument rather than as separate findings.
